name: Centre Passage, Double Pile
description: A through-passage front to back with two rooms either side, repeated above. The passage receives the visitor without admitting them to a room, carries the stair, and draws air through the house. Symmetry is not applied to this plan; it is generated by it, which is why the diagram survives every change of ornament laid over it. SERVICE STRIPPED 3 Sep 2026, per oq/the-parti-dissolved-its-own-dependencies (ruled 2 Sep) and OQ 40. This diagram named eleven enclosed ground rooms and a porch; its own three exemplars hold six enclosed spaces each where the count is established, and ALL THREE put their service in a basement, an outbuilding or a wing. Six service rooms -- butler's pantry, back hall, powder room, kitchen, pantry, breakfast room -- left the main block, which now holds porch, passage, stair, drawing room, dining room and library: five enclosed spaces plus the portico, against Gunston Hall's six. The service programme is not deleted, it is RELOCATED: it belongs in a dependency, which build/geometry.py can now place as a second massing element. Area was never the binding constraint here -- every sliver this diagram produced was inside its area band and outside its width or proportion band -- so no score term could have fixed it, and WP-9.4 measured that directly before this was ruled.

rooms.name: Centre Passage
rooms.note: Doors at both ends. A passage closed at the back is a corridor and loses the reason the type exists.

rooms.name: Principal Bath
rooms.note: Stacked over `butlers` until 3 Sep 2026, when the service programme left the main block (oq/the-parti-dissolved-its-own-dependencies). The claim is dropped rather than re-pointed: what remains below is the drawing room, the dining room and the library, and a bath stacked over a formal room is worse practice than the alignment it would replace. The stack wants the dependency's own wet rooms, which is a claim this diagram cannot make until a parti can name a room in another block.

scaling.note: Grows to seven bays and then wants dependencies rather than more width. Beyond about 5,000 sf the passage becomes a corridor and the diagram stops working.

trades_away: Circulation area — the passage is roughly a tenth of the plan and holds no furniture. In exchange it buys reception without intrusion, cross ventilation, and a facade that composes itself.
sources: Waterman, The Dwellings of Colonial America
Glassie, Folk Housing in Middle Virginia
